facts.heading: Exhausted since October
facts.content: Daniel has been completely burnt out since October. He works as a project manager at a logistics company.
facts.evidence: I've been completely burnt out since October.

facts.heading: Work schedule interferes with sleep
facts.content: Daniel stays up late thinking about work. This affects his sleep schedule.
facts.evidence: I'm at my desk by 7 and I'm still answering messages at 10 at night.

facts.heading: Poor sleep quality
facts.content: Daniel's sleep is terrible. He sleeps about four hours most nights.
facts.evidence: Most nights I sleep about 4 hours.

facts.heading: Sleep waking time
facts.content: Daniel wakes up at 3 in the morning and cannot get back to sleep.
facts.evidence: I wake up at 3 in the morning and just can't fall back asleep.

facts.heading: Work demands interrupt sleep
facts.content: Daniel has to start shipping schedules and check clients when he wakes up.
facts.evidence: We have to start shipping schedules, the clients, whether I've forgotten something.

facts.heading: Dreading the nights
facts.content: Daniel has started dreading the nights.
facts.evidence: I've started dreading the nights, if I'm honest.

facts.heading: Father's Parkinson's diagnosis
facts.content: Daniel's father was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.
facts.evidence: He was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.

facts.heading: Father's physical symptoms
facts.content: Daniel's father's hands shake and he is slower.
facts.evidence: His hands shake. He's slower.

facts.heading: Father's emotional state
facts.content: Daniel's father gets frustrated and is always being the strong one.
facts.evidence: He gets frustrated. He's having a dream and he's always being the strong one.

facts.heading: Daniel manages father's care
facts.content: Daniel drives his father to the hospital and leads appointments.
facts.evidence: I'm the one who drives him to the hospital and leads.

facts.heading: Caregiver burden and guilt
facts.content: Daniel feels guilty about his role in his father's care. He feels selfish being tired.
facts.evidence: Guilty for even saying it. It feels selfish to be tired when he's the one who is ill.

facts.heading: Sister lives in Toronto
facts.content: Daniel's sister Hannah lives in Toronto.
facts.evidence: My hungry sister Hannah lives in Toronto.

facts.heading: Sister's role in care
facts.content: Hannah calls his father every Sunday but is not neglecting him.
facts.evidence: She calls him every Sunday. She's not the one who's neglecting him.

facts.heading: Daniel avoids expressing feelings
facts.content: Daniel does not tell anyone about his feelings.
facts.evidence: So I don't say anything to anyone.

facts.heading: Daniel answers 'fine'
facts.content: When Hannah asks how he is, Daniel says fine.
facts.evidence: She asks how I am, and I say fine.

facts.heading: GP tests normal
facts.content: Daniel's GP did blood tests which were all normal. The GP said it is stress and exhaustion.
facts.evidence: She did blood tests. They were all normal. She said it's stress and exhaustion.

facts.heading: Claire is patient
facts.content: Claire is very patient with Daniel. She makes him tea and does not push him to talk.
facts.evidence: She's very patient. She makes me tea and doesn't push me to talk.

facts.heading: Claire seems hurt
facts.content: Daniel sees that Claire is wearing a hurt.
facts.evidence: But I can see she's wearing that hurt too.

facts.heading: Claire stopped asking about weekend
facts.content: Claire stopped asking if Daniel wanted to go away for the weekend.
facts.evidence: She stopped asking if I want to go away for the weekend because I always said no.

facts.heading: Emails cause stress
facts.content: The emails are a source of stress for Daniel. He worries about responding to them.
facts.evidence: The emails. And if I'm away I'll come back to 200 of them.

facts.heading: Rest has a price
facts.content: Daniel feels that rest has a cost. He cannot remember the last time he was properly off.
facts.evidence: So even rest has a price. Can't remember the last time I was properly off.

facts.heading: Ran for six years
facts.content: Daniel ran every Saturday morning for six years.
facts.evidence: I've done it for six years.

facts.heading: Stopped running two months ago
facts.content: Daniel stopped running about two months ago. His legs feel like lead now.
facts.evidence: I stopped about two months ago. My legs feel like lead.

facts.heading: Lost a part of self
facts.content: Daniel feels like he has lost a part of himself. He feels this loss is significant.
facts.evidence: Like I've lost a part of myself.

facts.heading: Relationship with boss Pearson
facts.content: Daniel's relationship with his boss Pearson is described. Pearson sends emails late at night and expects immediate answers.
facts.evidence: Pearson. He's alright as a person, but he sends emails at 11 at night and expects an answer before breakfast.

facts.heading: Answers emails immediately
facts.content: Daniel answers emails every time, even when he is in bed. Claire hates this.
facts.evidence: I answer it. Every time. Even if I'm on bed. Claire hates it.

facts.heading: Fear of job loss
facts.content: Daniel is afraid of being let go due to a restructuring this spring.
facts.evidence: There's a restructuring this spring and I'm afraid they'll let me go.

facts.heading: Relief and guilt about job loss
facts.content: Daniel thinks he might feel relieved if he is let go, but he would also feel horrible about it.
facts.evidence: I think part of me would be relieved. I'd feel horrible about being relieved.

facts.heading: Moved apart from third miss
facts.content: Daniel has moved apart from the third miss a lot, mostly inherited.
facts.evidence: A lot, mostly. Inheritable.

facts.heading: Panic attack symptoms
facts.content: Daniel experienced a physical event while moving apart from the third miss. He felt hurry and his hand was shaking.
facts.evidence: Hurry was going and my hand was shaking. We thought for a second it was a heart attack, but it passed.

facts.heading: Past frightening experience
facts.content: Daniel has experienced frightening episodes couple of times. One occurred on a train to Manchester.
facts.evidence: Couple of times. Once on a train to Manchester, just to get off and stand on a platform.

facts.heading: Fear of losing control
facts.content: Daniel fears losing control or ending up coping.
facts.evidence: That I'm losing it? That I'm gonna end up like, I don't know, coping?

facts.heading: Coffee consumption habit
facts.content: Daniel drinks about six cups of coffee a day. He has started having one in the evenings.
facts.evidence: I want about six cups a day and I've started having one in the evenings

facts.heading: Alcohol use for coping
facts.content: Daniel drinks two to three glasses of wine. He uses it for an hour, but wakes up anyway.
facts.evidence: Two glasses, sometimes three. How do you feel about the wine? Easy. It works for an hour. I wake up three anyway.

facts.heading: Wine perceived function
facts.content: Daniel feels the wine is not helping and feels like he is listing problems.
facts.evidence: It doesn't feel useful. It feels like I'm listing everything that's wrong with me.

facts.heading: Carrying burdens at night
facts.content: Daniel thinks he carries burdens during the nights.
facts.evidence: The nights, I think. If I could sleep, I could probably go put the rest.

facts.heading: Grandfather's behavior pattern
facts.content: Daniel's grandfather never complained about anything. He just got on with it.
facts.evidence: He never complained about anything. Not once. Just get on with it.

facts.heading: Daniel's self-perception
facts.content: Daniel thinks he is not weak. He feels very tired.
facts.evidence: That I'm not weak. I'm just very tired.

facts.heading: Difficulty believing self-talk
facts.content: Daniel is unsure if he believes the thought that he is not weak.
facts.evidence: I don't know if I believe it yet.

facts.heading: Proposed small behavioral change
facts.content: Daniel is willing to try a very small change to fix time in the evening.
facts.evidence: Very small. Fix time in the evening when you switch off your phone. Even for 20 minutes.

facts.heading: Proposed time for change
facts.content: Daniel suggested trying to fix time around half past nine.
facts.evidence: Yeah, half past nine, perhaps.

facts.heading: Proposed location for change
facts.content: Daniel suggested going to Dango's Glare at the other sofa.
facts.evidence: I could make it at Dango's Glare, the other sofa.

facts.heading: Current feeling after session
facts.content: Daniel feels tired but lighter after discussing things.
facts.evidence: Tired but lighter. It's normal to feel a bit shaky after saying all that.

facts.heading: Agreed to next session
facts.content: Daniel agreed to have the next session the following week.
facts.evidence: Same time next week? Yeah, I'll be here.
